Take Molisch’s reagent using a dropper.
Add about 6 drops of Molisch’s reagent into a test tube containing 2ml aqueous solution of glucose.

A red violet ring is produced at the junction of the two layers (acid layer and test layer) indicating the presence of carbohydrates.

Take 2 ml of Fehling’s solution A using a plastic dropper.
Add it to 2ml aqueous solution of glucose taken in a test tube.
Then add 2ml of Fehling’s solution B into the test tube. The solution turns deep blue colour.
Remove the test tube from the rack using a test tube holder.
Place it in a boiling water bath.
A reddish precipitate is formed in the glucose solution, indicating the presence of reducing sugar.

Remove the test tube from the rack using a test tube holder.

The colour remains the same. The test is negative, indicating that sucrose is not a reducing sugar.
